channel.title: Blockheight
channel.description: Blockheight reports crypto news: Bitcoin and Ethereum, DeFi protocols, exchanges, stablecoins, regulation, security incidents and market structure.

item.title: chainslist can add an EVM network to a wallet in one click
item.description: chainslist lists EVM chain IDs and RPC endpoints and lets users add a network to a wallet in one click, while checking the selected chain remains essential.

item.title: CFTC Seeks Comment on Leveraged Retail Crypto Rules
item.description: The CFTC seeks comment on a federal framework for leveraged retail crypto trades, including a tailored exchange category and a 60-day response window.

item.title: Wormhole bridge transfers: how to move tokens across chains
item.description: A wormhole bridge moves tokens between chains through a signed message; this guide explains route choice, destination addresses, token forms and transfer completion.

item.title: FinCEN withdraws $10,000 crypto wallet reporting proposal
item.description: FinCEN withdrew its dormant proposal to require reports on crypto transfers above $10,000 involving self-hosted wallets, ending a six-year rulemaking.

item.title: Fairshake backs 32 House candidates as crypto bill stalls
item.description: Fairshake says it will back 32 House candidates, including six with $1 million each, as the stalled CLARITY Act leaves crypto policy unresolved before November’s midterms.

item.title: How to Read an Avalanche Liquidity Position NFT
item.description: An Avalanche liquidity position NFT records a pool share, price range and claim rights; read its token pair, range, liquidity and fees before changing it.

item.title: Three Checks That Limit Sandwich Risk on Destination Swaps
item.description: Destination swaps face sandwich risk when a public trade can be reordered; a firm output floor, a liquid route and private submission narrow the exposure.

item.title: Tether-Backed Utexo Plans USDT Return to Bitcoin in October
item.description: Tether-backed Utexo plans to issue USDT on Bitcoin this month using RGB, adding private transfers and direct BTC swaps to the stablecoin’s network options.

item.title: What a Liquidity Lock Expiry Does to a Crypto Pool
item.description: A liquidity lock expiry releases the provider’s pool tokens; it does not withdraw assets or empty the pool. The holder must still submit a withdrawal transaction.

item.title: How to repay a USDC loan backed by AVAX in five steps
item.description: Repaying a USDC loan backed by AVAX means sourcing USDC or swapping collateral, checking the updated debt and health factor, then withdrawing only released AVAX.

item.title: TRON swap quotes can change before execution
item.description: A TRON swap quote estimates output from pool reserves at one moment; trade size, fees, routing and confirmation delay can change the amount that settles.

item.title: Set slippage deliberately for repeat Avalanche swaps
item.description: For repeat Avalanche swaps, use a slippage limit that reflects the token’s liquidity, then check minimum output and execution results before reusing it.

item.title: Who Can Recover a Misrouted Chainflip Swap?
item.description: A wrong Chainflip destination usually leaves recovery to the address controller; failed payouts follow a separate fallback path, with limits on where and how long it works.

item.title: Ethereum Foundation puts private API payments on mainnet
item.description: Ethereum Foundation and Open Anonymity put zkAPI on mainnet Oct. 1, separating AI API payments from identity while leaving prompts and IP addresses visible.

item.title: When to withdraw liquidity from a Base pool
item.description: Withdraw when expected pool fees no longer justify token-price exposure, your position leaves its range, or you need the capital; check returns before exiting.

item.title: How to Record Omnichain Swaps for Portfolio Attribution
item.description: A cross-chain swap spans separate transactions, so portfolio records must join source debits, bridge delivery and destination trades before assigning cost basis.

item.title: How to Use XMR as Loan Collateral
item.description: XMR can back a loan through a custodial lender or a wrapped token in DeFi, but each route changes who controls collateral and what can trigger its loss.

item.title: Estimate impermanent loss before adding liquidity
item.description: Use the entry-to-current price ratio to estimate an LP position’s loss against holding, then assess fees, incentives and liquidity ranges separately.

item.title: XMR Bridge Deposit Confirmations: How the Wait Works
item.description: XMR deposits pass from wallet broadcast to Monero confirmation, then wait for the bridge’s own threshold before the destination asset is released.

item.title: Paying an onchain freelancer from Monero
item.description: Paying an onchain freelancer from Monero means converting XMR into the asset and network in the invoice, then checking delivery and documenting the swap.
